panels.description:
TrainingPeaks canonical Efficiency Factor: mean(GradeAdjustedSpeed) / mean(HR) x 100.

METHOD
• GradeAdjustedSpeed (Garmin GAP/NGP) normalizes for terrain grade
• mean(GAP) / mean(HR), not mean(GAP/HR) — per TrainingPeaks spec
• First 10 min excluded (HR stabilization per Friel)
• Speed > 0.5 m/s (exclude stops)
• No HR zone filter — full workout EF, compare similar session types

HOW TO READ
• Higher = faster at lower cardiac cost = better aerobic fitness
• Rising trend over 4-8 weeks = confirmed aerobic adaptation
• Orange line = 7-day moving average

Ref: TrainingPeaks EF, Joe Friel (2009), Coggan/Allen power-based training.

targets.query: SELECT mean("GradeAdjustedSpeed") * 100.0 / mean("HeartRate") AS "val" FROM "ActivityGPS" WHERE $timeFilter AND "ActivitySelector" =~ /running/ AND "DurationSeconds" >= 600 AND "Speed" > 0.5 GROUP BY time(1d) fill(null)

panels.description:
Cardiac-efficiency progression - pace at fixed HR, monthly average (30d).

3 NON-overlapping average-HR bands: ~140 (easy, 135-144 bpm) | ~150 (steady, 145-154) | ~160 (tempo, 155-164). Each point = 1000 / mean(speed) of flat runs whose mean HR falls in the band, aggregated over 30 days. Bands <135 and >=165 removed (2-5 runs, too noisy).

Y axis: pace mm:ss/km (lower = faster). Terrain filter: D+/km < 25. Distance > 1 km.

FIX vs old version: non-overlapping bins (no more double-counting at the boundaries), only the 3 bands that carry data, and monthly smoothing (no more raw-point spaghetti).

WEATHER CONFOUNDER WARNING: over a Dec->May window, pace at fixed HR RISES (slows down) mainly because of rising heat, NOT a loss of fitness - at free pace the athlete slows when it's hot (see 'Heat impact' panel #120). Heat-corrected version: EF vs WBGT (#120) and EF GAP/HR (#300, this dashboard). Read the trend while keeping the season in mind.

targets.query: SELECT 1000 / MEAN("averageSpeed") AS "~140 (easy)" FROM "ActivitySummary" WHERE $timeFilter AND "ActivitySelector" =~ /running/ AND "distance" > 1000 AND "elevationGain" * 1000 < "distance" * 25 AND "averageHR" >= 135 AND "averageHR" < 145 GROUP BY time(30d) fill(none)

SELECT 1000 / MEAN("averageSpeed") AS "~150 (steady)" FROM "ActivitySummary" WHERE $timeFilter AND "ActivitySelector" =~ /running/ AND "distance" > 1000 AND "elevationGain" * 1000 < "distance" * 25 AND "averageHR" >= 145 AND "averageHR" < 155 GROUP BY time(30d) fill(none)

SELECT 1000 / MEAN("averageSpeed") AS "~160 (tempo)" FROM "ActivitySummary" WHERE $timeFilter AND "ActivitySelector" =~ /running/ AND "distance" > 1000 AND "elevationGain" * 1000 < "distance" * 25 AND "averageHR" >= 155 AND "averageHR" < 165 GROUP BY time(30d) fill(none)

panels.title: Pace @ fixed HR - monthly trend, 3 bands (flat runs, D+/km < 25)

panels.description:
Pace vs HR scatter - each point = 1 flat run (D+/km < 25, 180d). X = average HR (cardiac effort), Y = pace mm:ss/km (lower = faster). COLOR = recency (gradient): blue = old (~6 months) -> yellow -> red = recent.

HOW TO READ: at a given HR, if the red points (recent) are LOWER (faster) than the blue ones (old) = gain in cardiac efficiency. If they rise = a cost. Here the recent cloud rises mainly because of rising heat (Dec->May, see #120) - this is not a fitness regression.

Advantage vs binning: no arbitrary boundaries or double-counting, each run appears once and you see the full HR<->pace relationship.

targets.query: SELECT "averageHR" AS "HR", 1000 / "averageSpeed" AS "Pace" FROM "ActivitySummary" WHERE $timeFilter AND time < now() - 540d AND "ActivitySelector" =~ /running/ AND "averageHR" > 110 AND "distance" > 1000 AND "elevationGain" * 1000 < "distance" * 25

SELECT "averageHR" AS "HR", 1000 / "averageSpeed" AS "Pace" FROM "ActivitySummary" WHERE $timeFilter AND time >= now() - 540d AND time < now() - 180d AND "ActivitySelector" =~ /running/ AND "averageHR" > 110 AND "distance" > 1000 AND "elevationGain" * 1000 < "distance" * 25

SELECT "averageHR" AS "HR", 1000 / "averageSpeed" AS "Pace" FROM "ActivitySummary" WHERE $timeFilter AND time >= now() - 180d AND "ActivitySelector" =~ /running/ AND "averageHR" > 110 AND "distance" > 1000 AND "elevationGain" * 1000 < "distance" * 25

panels.title: Pace vs avg HR - colored by recency (flat runs, D+/km < 25)
Heat impact — Efficiency Factor vs WBGT
panels.description:
Real impact of heat on physiology. Each point = 1 run (365d). X = WBGT (heat-stress index: integrates temperature + humidity + sun + wind). Y = Efficiency Factor = speed/HR (m.min-1/bpm), higher = more efficient.

Why EF and not HR: at free pace the athlete slows when it's hot, so average HR does not rise (effect ~ 0 bpm/degC at equal pace). The cost of heat shows up in EFFICIENCY: EF drops ~0.32%/degC (EF~WBGT p=0.004, n=92). Cloud sloping down to the right = heat impact.

WBGT zones: <18 low / 18-23 moderate / 23-28 high / >28 extreme. Performance optimum ~8-15 degC.
Limits: few runs >25 degC; mostly easy/steady runs; pace is self-selected (the cost also appears as lost pace, not only in EF).

targets.query: SELECT ("averageSpeed" * 60 / "averageHR") AS "EF" FROM "ActivitySummary" WHERE $timeFilter AND "ActivitySelector" =~ /running/ AND "averageHR" > 80 AND "averageHR" < 210 AND "averageSpeed" > 1.5 AND "averageSpeed" < 6.5
SELECT "wbgt_estimated" AS "WBGT" FROM "ActivityWeather" WHERE $timeFilter
